reasoning: ScopeTree is a strong runtime and supervision-system metaphor, but its broad scenario lead may overfit one technical implementation lens. Retain it as subsystem or category vocabulary unless the public product center is explicitly a scope tree.

Faultcell makes bounded failure concrete, but it describes one distributed-runtime mechanism more naturally than the full program, evaluation, and optimization system. Preserve it as subsystem vocabulary rather than assuming a master-brand role.

Processloom strongly evokes concurrent BEAM work but can narrow the product theory to runtime composition. Retain it as a subsystem or category candidate and require separate evidence before using it as a company or protocol identity.

Faultglass is legible for inspection of failure boundaries, but that is a narrower claim than the complete public API and research horizon. Keep it available for observability or runtime tooling instead of promoting it automatically to the umbrella identity.

Draftifact is unusually apt as a category noun for versioned generated artifacts. That category strength does not by itself establish company, community, or protocol fit, so those roles must be evaluated separately.

Evidence Loop truthfully describes a bounded evaluation and repair cycle, but it is more immediately a method or category descriptor than a distinctive umbrella brand. Preserve that role instead of treating rank as architecture proof.

Pinned Lineage precisely names reproducible provenance, but it foregrounds one artifact property. Keep it as feature, subsystem, or research vocabulary unless the final identity is intentionally centered on lineage.

The dotted public surface becomes beam_run and BeamRun in important code projections, losing its intended grammar. Do not advance it as the master identity without an explicit, tested package and namespace contract.

Run.Pack collapses to run_pack and RunPack on package and module surfaces. Its punctuation promise is not portable enough for a public master identity until the exact code contract is chosen and tested.

GenLine projects to Genline under ordinary Elixir casing, weakening the intended generation-lineage reading. Hold it from the master-name frontier unless that loss is accepted in a concrete namespace prototype.

Footlight is evocative but does little unaided work to explain programs, evidence, evaluation, or optimization. Hold it from a general master-brand decision unless listener and newcomer sessions show that the metaphor carries the intended category.

Axima has substantial profile disagreement and lacks human pronunciation evidence. Its sound and possible axiom or proof association require a blind listener gate before it can be treated as a robust abstract brand.

Solfa names regionally variable music-pedagogy traditions and currently has no human language or cultural validation. Keep it visible, but do not advance it through a global identity decision without qualified review.
Epistemic Review Board implies governance, mandate, and review authority that the project does not possess. Preserve it as a speculative process concept, not a public institutional identity.
Maybe Better makes uncertainty and measured comparison unusually explicit. Retain it for a descriptor, campaign, or method track even if its humility is too weak for the eventual master brand.

The Margins gives feedback, uncertainty, and minority interpretation a memorable place in the artifact model. Retain it as editorial, community, or review vocabulary even if it does not lead scalar scenario ranks.

Measuremark joins evidence and durable program artifacts without claiming that every score is truth. Preserve it in the descriptor and category track even if an abstract master brand is chosen elsewhere.
Repair Loop communicates bounded observation, feedback, and correction without magical improvement claims. Retain it as method or lifecycle vocabulary regardless of master-brand outcome.

Programmatics offers a broad research-category reading that is less tied to one runtime mechanism. Preserve it for the framework or discipline vocabulary track despite its existing associations and international-score disagreement.

Orsel remains useful as a comparatively brand-shaped alternative to the technically descriptive frontier. Keep it in a separate master-brand track subject to pronunciation, collision, and connotation gates.

Tervel provides a brand-shaped counterweight to runtime compounds. Preserve it in the master-brand track while treating the large international-behavior profile spread as a required human-review signal.

Caldrin should remain available as an abstract umbrella candidate so the final comparison is not dominated by generated technical compounds. It still requires the same listener, language, collision, and legal gates as every coined brand.
